correctness.rationale: For every n>=4, c,B>0, nonnegative independent edge conductances, the full-budget Kirchhoff index is strictly convex on the connected feasible region because the second directional derivative of Tr(L+J/N)^(-1) is strictly positive for any nonzero edge variation. Compactness with divergence at disconnection yields a unique optimizer; automorphisms force positive constant intra-layer and interlayer weights. The exact tensor-product spectrum 0, 2b, na (n-1), na+2b (n-1) yields the stated scalar equation. Unique sign-crossing of its derivative follows from strict convexity along the affine budget line. Rational scaling expansions prove all three limits with root trapping. The 202 deterministic test assertions from verify.py independently check formulas and budgets on sample inputs but are not used as infinite proof.

value.rationale: A perfect matching joining two dense communities is a canonical and natural interlayer design for resistance reduction. The explicit cost-dependent optimizer and quantitative budget fraction are directly interpretable, and the price-one transition separates constant interlayer investment from vanishing allocations with two different power-law exponents, n^(-1/3) and n^(-1/2). These formulas do not follow from correctness or reproducibility alone and give specific network-design insight rather than an arbitrary finite computation.
